title: 1. Hook: The Mystery of the Buzzing City
text: In ancient Indian texts like Ayurveda, Madhu (Honey) is celebrated as a powerful medicine, and bees were deeply respected for their hard work. Have you ever wondered how these tiny creatures build huge, perfect honeycombs? Let's meet Anita Khushwaha, a real-life 'Girl Star' from Bihar, who uncovered the secrets of the bees and changed her life!

content.title: 2. Socratic Thinking: The Bee Hierarchy
content.text: Why do you think only certain bees collect nectar while others stay in the hive? Imagine if a school had no principal, teachers, or helpers—would it run smoothly? How do you think bees organize their work?

content.title: 3. Discovery: Inside the Bee City
content.description: A beehive is like a bustling city! The Queen is the mayor who lays all the eggs, the Workers are the busy citizens building the hive and collecting food, and the Drones are the special guests. Notice the hexagonal shape of their homes—it's the most efficient shape in nature!

title: 4. Reveal: Roles of the Bees
text: Anita learned that every hive has one Queen Bee whose only job is to lay eggs. Most bees in the hive are Worker Bees. They are the true heroes—they clean, build the hive, care for baby bees, and fly far to collect Nectar (Sweet Liquid). The male bees, called Drones, have no special role in the daily work.

content.definition: The sweet liquid produced by flowers, which bees collect to make honey.
A place where bees are kept; a collection of beehives.

content.question: Which bee in the hive is responsible for doing almost all the work, including collecting nectar and building the honeycomb?

content.title: 6. Reflection: Anita's Struggle for Education
content.text: Anita had to fight with her parents just to go to school because they believed girls shouldn't study. She taught young children to pay her own school fees. Take a moment to reflect: Why is education so important for everyone? How did learning mathematics and science at school help Anita calculate her profits in beekeeping?

title: 7. Connection: Social Insects
text: Did you know? Just like honeybees live and work together in a highly organized colony, ants, termites, and wasps also live in groups! They share a 'social' structure, much like human societies where everyone has a specific job to help the community survive.

content.title: 8. Mastery Challenge: Become an Apiarist!
content.text: Mini Challenge: Draw a honeycomb pattern (hint: it's made of hexagons!) and label the three types of bees inside it. Then, explain to your parents or a friend what each bee does in the 'bee city'.

content.title: Common Misconception: Who lays the eggs?
content.text: Many people think all bees in a hive lay eggs. Actually, ONLY the Queen Bee lays eggs! The thousands of other bees you see outside are worker bees who cannot lay eggs.
